Doctor: Have you had any prior episodes of similar pain, and have you been diagnosed with kidney stones, urinary tract infections, or gallstones in the past? Patient: Yes, I've had kidney stones before, but I've been able to pass them. This one is taking a lot longer, though. Doctor: Have you experienced any fever, chills, or changes in urinary frequency or volume associated with the pain? Patient: I haven't had a fever or chills, and I don't notice any significant changes in how often I urinate, just that it burns a little when I do. Doctor: Have you undergone any imaging studies, such as a CT scan or ultrasound, for this current episode of pain? If so, what were the findings? Patient: I saw my doctor, and they ordered a CT scan, which showed a kidney stone in the right ureter. They sent me to see a urologist after that. Doctor
